title: A Tryouts for the Prom
premise: Noor Almeida, a baker's son who channels everything he can't say into bread, is paired with his nemesis, sharp-tongued Ivy Chen, for a semester project documenting the history of their school's scholarship fund. Digging through archives, they discover the fund was quietly redirected decades ago by the founding family — Ivy's family — to buy influence, and that Noor's own scholarship exists only because his late grandmother once covered for them. When the truth threatens Ivy's college future and Noor's place at the school, both must decide whether survival is worth complicity. At prom, Noor tells the truth publicly, losing his best friend Marcus but gaining something harder: a self he doesn't have to swallow.
about_author: Petra Blackwood grew up above her parents' bakery, where she learned that people confess things to strangers over warm bread. She writes stories about teenagers who inherit more than they asked for.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. He counts down the 94 days to graduation while working the bakery counter at dawn, baking a 'sorry' loaf he can't deliver to his estranged best friend Marcus. Establishes bread-as-language motif and the suffocating feeling that his life is a sentence being served. Beat: restless dread.

chapters.title: Assigned Seating
chapters.summary: Mr. Okonkwo announces the semester-long local history project and pairs Noor with Ivy Chen, his academic rival since freshman year. Ivy publicly mocks the bakery; Noor snaps back. Neither can switch. Beat: humiliation sharpened into defiance.

chapters.title: Ivy, Annotated
chapters.summary: Ivy's POV. We see her gilded pressure at home — her grandmother Ruth Chen is a school benefactor whose portrait hangs in the atrium. Ivy resents being a 'legacy.' She chooses their project topic: the Whitfield Scholarship Fund, founded 1968. Beat: ambition masking resentment.

chapters.title: Flour and Archives
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Forced collaboration begins badly in the school archive until Noor notices Ivy actually reads everything, footnotes and all. They find a gap: the fund's ledger jumps from 1974 to 1976, two years missing. Beat: grudging respect, first crack in the wall.

chapters.title: What Marcus Knows
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Marcus, now orbiting wealthy seniors, warns Noor off the scholarship research — 'some things are load-bearing.' Their frozen friendship thaws slightly, painfully. Noor bakes a reconciliation loaf; Marcus leaves it untouched. Beat: aching hope.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At home, Noor finds his late grandmother Rosa's recipe box and discovers a 1975 letter tucked inside: she once worked for the Chen family and references 'the arrangement.' His scholarship isn't charity — it's hush money's descendant. Beat: vertigo.

chapters.title: Ruth Chen's Parlor
chapters.summary: Ivy's POV. Ivy interviews her grandmother for the project. Ruth is charming and evasive, but Ivy catches a flicker when the missing years come up. Ruth warns her: 'Families survive by agreeing on one story.' Beat: loyalty beginning to sour.

chapters.title: Detention Bread
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A fight with Ivy in the archive gets them both detention, where they actually talk — about parents, pressure, the prom neither admits wanting. Noor brings bread; Ivy eats it and says nothing, which from her is a thank-you. Beat: intimacy by accident.

chapters.title: The Second Ledger
chapters.summary: Ivy's POV. In the county records office, Ivy finds the missing years: her family quietly redirected scholarship funds in 1975 to settle a scandal, and Rosa Almeida signed a confidentiality agreement in exchange for her grandson's future endowment. Ivy realizes Noor is the collateral. Beat: sickening clarity.

chapters.title: Two Truths, One Table
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Ivy shows Noor the ledger. He learns his whole life at the school was purchased by his grandmother's silence. Fury at Ivy, at Ruth, at Rosa, at himself. He storms out; the project — and something unspoken between them — hangs by a thread. Beat: betrayal.

chapters.title: Rising
chapters.summary: Ivy's POV. Ruth offers Ivy a deal: bury the finding, and her Columbia legacy admission is guaranteed. Ivy sees the machine clearly for the first time — how power recycles itself through children. She doesn't answer yet. Beat: the corruption offered, the price named.

chapters.title: Sourdough Confessions
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor rereads Rosa's letters and finds her real voice: she wasn't a coward, she was protecting a son with no options, and she hated it. Grief reframes anger. He bakes her recipe for the first time and it comes out right. Beat: forgiveness of the dead.

chapters.title: Prom Committee Politics
chapters.summary: Ivy's POV. Prom approaches as a stage: Ruth is the keynote patron, Marcus is on the committee, and the school plans a tribute to the Chen family's 'generosity.' Ivy realizes the tribute will happen the same night their project is due. Beat: converging timelines, dread.

chapters.title: The Almost
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Late night in the archive, exhausted, Noor and Ivy nearly kiss — then Ivy pulls back, saying she can't be another thing he loses. He realizes the project stopped being a project weeks ago. Beat: tenderness with a countdown attached.

chapters.title: Marcus's Bargain
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV (single departure). Marcus knows what the Chens did — his father works for their company — and has been keeping Noor close to keep him quiet. Ruth pressures him to confirm the tribute speech. He agrees, hating himself. Beat: the cost of survival, embodied.

chapters.title: Deadline Eve
chapters.summary: Ivy's POV. Ivy finishes the report with the full truth and two versions: the honest one and the safe one. Ruth finds the draft, and the mask drops — threats, cold arithmetic, a grandmother Ivy no longer recognizes. Ivy burns neither copy. Beat: the choice made real.

chapters.title: Prom Night: The Atrium
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Prom, under Ruth Chen's portrait. Marcus gives the tribute speech, smooth and hollow, and catches Noor's eye mid-lie. Ivy arrives alone. Noor holds the honest report in his jacket, feeling its weight like a loaf about to crack. Beat: held breath.

chapters.title: The Truth, Out Loud
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. When the principal praises the Chen legacy, Noor takes the mic and reads the 1975 ledger entry aloud — the redirected funds, Rosa's signature, his own bought scholarship. The room fractures. Ivy steps up beside him, unasked, and confirms it. Beat: the climax, costly and irreversible.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Parking Lot
chapters.summary: Ivy's POV. Fallout: Marcus's friendship with Noor shatters — 'you didn't just tell the truth, you told it at prom' — and Ivy's Columbia offer is 'under review.' In the parking lot, Noor and Ivy admit the almost out loud. Beat: grief and first honest love.

chapters.title: What Rosa Left Me
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The school board, embarrassed, restores the fund's original charter; Noor's scholarship survives on new, clean terms. He bakes Rosa's bread for Marcus, leaves it at his door with the full story in writing — truth offered without an audience this time. Beat: repair attempted.

chapters.title: Graduation
chapters.summary: Ivy's POV. Ivy declines the legacy safety net and takes a merit offer elsewhere. Ruth, publicly diminished, sends a single line: 'You chose the hard bread.' At graduation, Noor and Ivy sit together; Mr. Okonkwo gives their project an A and calls it 'the most honest history this school has produced.' Beat: inheritance refused, self claimed.

chapters.title: The First Loaf of Summer
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Epilogue. The bakery at dawn, no countdown anymore. Marcus shows up, eats the bread, says 'start over' — not forgiveness yet, but the door open. Noor bakes a loaf with no feeling hidden in it, just bread, and shares it with Ivy on the step. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
